title.narrative: Smart Urban Water Management: Enhancing the Adaptive Capacity and Urban Resilience of Amman through Urban Green Infrastructure

description.narrative:
This project addresses the increasing risk of flash floods in Amman, exacerbated by rapid urbanization, inadequate stormwater drainage systems, and climate change impacts. Flash floods have paralyzed Amman city in the past, causing loss of lives, infrastructure damage, and heightened vulnerabilities, particularly among the most vulnerable segments of the population. In 2018, 35 people lost their lives because of flash floods and an estimated 150,000 were affected by the floods, which sheds light on the seriousness of this problem. In February of 2019, severe rainfall caused an estimated maximum flow of 658m3/s, which led to severe flooding in Downtown Amman, resulting in damages and economic losses for local businesses and shops. According to the National Centre for Security and Crisis Management (2019), floods are the most frequent natural disaster in Jordan and have caused over 395 deaths and affected over 650,000 people since 1963. The Jordanian Civil Defence estimated that in the period between 1981-2012, the total economic losses caused by reported natural disasters (593 records) has reached an estimated US$29 million. With weather patterns indicating a high likelihood of recurring floods and storms in 2024, urgent action is imperative. In 2022, it was estimated that $7.5 billion is needed for mitigation interventions alone in Jordan. The project is aligned with national strategies emphasizing rainwater harvesting as a sustainable solution and recognizes the critical need to enhance the resilience of vulnerable communities against water-related challenges.
This project builds on previous collaborations between UN-Habitat Jordan and the Greater Amman Municipality (GAM) to address flood risks. Building on the Flood Risk Assessment and Flood Hazard Mapping of Downtown Amman, UN-Habitat identified 120 flood hotspots for short- and medium-term sustainable drainage interventions which are ideally spread all around the city for stormwater detention and retention either above or below the ground, including bio-retention and detention elements, filter strips, attenuation ponds, etc. The Al Zohour Green Triangle pilot project was implemented, which demonstrated sustainable stormwater management through innovative green infrastructure solutions inspired by Dutch best practices. Additionally, the project fosters knowledge exchange between Jordan and the Netherlands, promoting capacity building and the adoption of international best practices in sustainable urban drainage and stormwater management.
Accordingly, strategically leveraging UN-Habitat’s programming in Amman and in alignment with national and local priorities, this project aims to enhance an enabling environment to address water challenges through the development and implementation of smart urban water management systems in Amman city, with a focus on strengthening adaptive capacities and promoting sustainable water management measures. The integration between the key components of (1) the implementation of green infrastructure solutions to enhance city resilience; (2) public incentivization for active engagement and innovation in green development; and (3) knowledge exchange and capacity building initiatives; collectively creates an enabling environment for addressing water challenges in Amman comprehensively and sustainably. By strategically implementing short-term sustainable urban water management systems rooted in innovative green infrastructure solutions, the project will strengthen the city's resilience against water-related issues. Simultaneously, recognizing exemplary environmental initiatives and disseminating impactful awareness campaigns will endeavour to inspire widespread participation in sustainable practices among Jordanian residents. Additionally, through enhancing capacities among stakeholders and facilitating the exchange of best practices, the project promotes informed decision-making and cultivates sustainable water practices at all levels of governance. This integrated approach, which combines diverse capacities, community empowerment, and innovative technologies, establishes a resilient and adaptable framework for effective water management in the face of dynamic threats such as flash floods, water scarcity, and climate change impacts. Together, these integrated components create an enabling environment that catalyses a shift towards environmental consciousness and proactive engagement in sustainable water management practices, laying the groundwork for long-term resilience in Amman's water sector.
By tackling flash floods and water scarcity head-on, the project will empower decision-makers and communities with the knowledge and tools necessary to navigate these obstacles sustainably. Collaborative efforts and partnerships forged through this project will help foster social cohesion and stability among refugees and host communities, as well as support cross-city knowledge exchange.
